transcript.speaker: Heard
transcript.text: Hi, I’m Gogo. I’m building RoomPilot, a quiet assistant for live opportunity conversations.

transcript.speaker: Heard
transcript.text: I’m Camille. I work with founder programs around events, so this is exactly the room where that problem shows up.

transcript.speaker: Heard
transcript.text: The simple pitch is: people leave useful conversations with no clear next move.

transcript.speaker: Heard
transcript.text: Right. The hard part is not meeting people; it is remembering the useful next step before the moment disappears.

transcript.speaker: Heard
transcript.text: That is the pain. Most tools summarize later; RoomPilot helps while the person is still here.

transcript.speaker: Heard
transcript.text: Then the product should show the exact quote, say what it is not assuming, and give one useful next move.

transcript.speaker: Heard
transcript.text: What one action would save that moment in this room?

transcript.speaker: Heard
transcript.text: If someone says, ‘I’d talk to Hexa,’ capture that, then ask who at Hexa and what to mention.

transcript.speaker: Heard
transcript.text: So the tech path is simple: OpenAI Realtime turns speech into live text, Pioneer checks which quote is worth acting on, and RoomPilot turns it into one card.

transcript.speaker: Heard
transcript.text: And the memory graph matters only if it can connect this quote to something Sarah said yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Heard
transcript.text: Right: OpenAI gives us the live words, Pioneer stops every sentence from becoming a card, audio is not stored, and the UI keeps the proof visible.

transcript.speaker: Heard
transcript.text: That is the two-minute pitch: not another call summary, a proof-backed next-move layer for live rooms.

transcript.speaker: Heard
transcript.text: Perfect. That is exactly the story I want the judges to feel.

transcript.speaker: Heard
transcript.text: Good. Now make the demo quiet enough that the proof does the selling.
